To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a regime shift in the Baltic Sea occurred in 1993-1994, (ii) the regime shift was caused by climate-induced changes in the hydrography of the Baltic Sea, and (iii) this climate-induced shift was amplified by overfishing, which resulted in the collapse of the Baltic cod stock and the increase in the Baltic sprat stock.
(1) climate change and overfishing can cause regime shifts, and (2) the effects propagate through the food-web via a trophic cascade that is mediated by zooplankton.

the climate-induced changes in hydrographic conditions in the central Baltic Sea caused a regime shift in zooplankton composition, and that the change in zooplanktivory by sprat, caused by the regime shift in zooplanlton, resulted in a trophic cascade to fish, which amplified the regime shift in the zooplanktivorous fish species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the complex interplay between climate and anthropogenic forcing in the Baltic Sea ecosystem.
the effects of climate and overexploitation on the dynamics of the zooplanktivorous fish stock and on the zooplanktontrophic level.
the dynamics of a simple ecosystem, which is highly vulnerable to climate-induced and anthropogenic pressures.

the Baltic Sea is currently undergoing a regime shift from a cod-dominated to a sprat-dominated ecosystem.
the ecosystem is currently in a new regime, and that this is a direct effect of climate change.
climate change and overfishing are both important and act synergistically, and that the effects of overfishing are amplified by climate change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
zooplankton is a key link in the foodweb and that the effects of climate change on the ecosystem can be amplified by overfishing.
climate change is a major driver of the Baltic Sea ecosystem, which can be amplified by anthropogenic effects, such as overfishing.

the climate regime shift in the Baltic Sea caused an ecological regime shift with changes in the ecosystem structure and functioning, and that overfishing of the piscivorous fish species cod amplified these effects.

the effects of climate and over-fishing are not independent, but act together to cause regime shifts in the ecosystem.
climate and fishing interact to cause regime shifts in ecosystems.
